summary: iter70 — 34/34 backend tests PASS (3 new iter70 enroll-begin origin tests + 31 regression: iter63/66/67/68/69). Frontend signup screen renders biometric-enrollment-field with both bio-webauthn-btn and bio-iris-btn. Clicking iris opens iris-fullscreen-wizard (data-testid OK), header 'Identification iris' + cancel X + iris-status footer all present. Camera-denied path shows exact spec message 'Impossible d'accéder à la caméra. Vérifie les permissions et recommence.' iris-cancel closes the wizard. WebAuthn enroll-begin with body.origin returns options.rp.id == window.location.origin host (chain verified end-to-end). ONE BLOCKING UX BUG FOUND: the iris-fullscreen-wizard is NOT actually fullscreen on signup — it renders at 446×996 inside the login card (viewport is 1280×900). Root cause: the parent login card div carries `backdrop-blur-xl` which compiles to `backdrop-filter: blur(...)` — per CSS spec, any non-`none` backdrop-filter on an ancestor establishes a *containing block* for ALL descendants including position:fixed ones. So `fixed inset-0 z-[110]` is trapped to the card. Fix: render IrisFullscreenWizard through a React Portal (ReactDOM.createPortal to document.body).

ui_bugs.issue: Wizard renders at 446×996px instead of the full viewport (1280×900) on the signup screen. `fixed inset-0 z-[110]` is constrained because the parent Login card uses `backdrop-blur-xl` (= `backdrop-filter: blur(...)`) which creates a containing block for all descendants — including position:fixed. The user explicitly requested 'Iris fullscreen au lieu de petite fenêtre' in iter70 deliverable #2; this fix is therefore NOT effective on the signup page. The wizard IS visually centered and looks like a 'small window', exactly the bug iter70 set out to fix. Resolution: wrap the wizard's return in ReactDOM.createPortal(<wizard>, document.body) so it escapes the backdrop-filter containing block. Quick confirmation: removing `backdrop-blur-xl` from the Login card (or adding the portal) makes the wizard fill 1280×900.

rca of the issue:
ROOT CAUSE: iter70 deliverable #2 (fullscreen iris wizard) is defeated by a CSS containing-block side-effect of `backdrop-blur-xl` on the parent Login card. Per W3C Filter Effects spec, any element with `backdrop-filter: ` becomes the containing block for its position:fixed descendants. The wizard's `fixed inset-0` is therefore anchored to the 446px-wide blurred card, not the viewport. REPRODUCTION: open /login → click 'Sign up' → click 'Iris (webcam)' → measure [data-testid='iris-fullscreen-wizard'].getBoundingClientRect() — actual width≈446 vs expected 1280. , document.body)`. This sidesteps every CSS containing-block trap (transform, filter, contain, perspective, will-change) by rendering the wizard as a direct child of . Took ~15 lines.
